answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake in a vault before it may transact, with the stake slashed on proven fraud. Reputation then grows like a vine, branching only through verified work history, so a fresh fake identity starts at zero and must pay real compute and time costs to climb. At the zenith of trust, high-value tasks demand both stake and history, making mass fake identities economically irrational.
